events.title: Wang Geon becomes king and founds the Goryeo dynasty
events.description: Wang Geon, a general of Taebong, was made king of Goryeo by the generals who had overthrown Gung Ye. As Taejo he accepted Silla's surrender in 935 and defeated Later Baekje in 936, reuniting the Korean peninsula.
events.html: Wang Geon, a general of Taebong, was made king of Goryeo by the generals who had overthrown Gung Ye. As Taejo he accepted Silla's surrender in 935 and defeated Later Baekje in 936, reuniting the Korean peninsula.

events.title: Eleanor of Aquitaine marries the future Louis VII of France
events.description: Archbishop Geoffrey of Bordeaux oversaw the wedding of Eleanor of Aquitaine and Prince Louis in the Cathedral of Saint-André in Bordeaux. Immediately afterwards the couple were enthroned as duke and duchess of Aquitaine.

events.title: Afonso Henriques wins the Battle of Ourique
events.description: Afonso Henriques defeated an Almoravid army at Ourique and was soon styling himself King of Portugal. The victory became a founding legend of Portuguese independence from León.
events.html: Afonso Henriques defeated an Almoravid army at Ourique and was soon styling himself King of Portugal. The victory became a founding legend of Portuguese independence from León.

events.title: Nicaean forces under Alexios Strategopoulos recapture Constantinople
events.description: Alexios Strategopoulos, a general of the Empire of Nicaea, led Nicaean forces to recapture Constantinople, held by the Latin Empire since the Fourth Crusade of 1204. The recapture ended the Latin Empire and restored the Byzantine Empire.

events.title: Henry IV of France converts to Catholicism
events.description: The Protestant Henry IV abjured his faith at the basilica of Saint-Denis to win acceptance from Catholic France. The words 'Paris is well worth a Mass' are attributed to him, and he entered Paris the next year.
events.html: The Protestant Henry IV abjured his faith at the basilica of Saint-Denis to win acceptance from Catholic France. The words 'Paris is well worth a Mass' are attributed to him, and he entered Paris the next year.

events.title: Cooke and Wheatstone demonstrate the electric telegraph
events.description: William Cooke and Charles Wheatstone sent messages along a telegraph line between Euston and Camden Town in London. Its success led to the first commercial telegraph on the Great Western Railway.
events.html: William Cooke and Charles Wheatstone sent messages along a telegraph line between Euston and Camden Town in London. Its success led to the first commercial telegraph on the Great Western Railway.

events.title: Louise Brown, the first 'test-tube baby', is born
events.description: Louise Brown was born in Oldham, the first person conceived by in vitro fertilisation, pioneered by Robert Edwards and Patrick Steptoe. Millions of people have since been born through IVF.
events.html: Louise Brown was born in Oldham, the first person conceived by in vitro fertilisation, pioneered by Robert Edwards and Patrick Steptoe. Millions of people have since been born through IVF.

events.title: Svetlana Savitskaya becomes the first woman to walk in space
events.description: Soviet cosmonaut Svetlana Savitskaya spent three and a half hours outside the Salyut 7 space station. She tested a hand-held tool for cutting and welding metal in space.
